title: CONNECT-UDP URI Template and Target Architecture
purpose: Define RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP URI Template validation, default template construction, target host/port validation, IPv6 literal encoding, and request path/query expansion.
design_summary: `Http3ConnectUdpUriTemplate` validates absolute printable-ASCII URI Templates, rejects forbidden level 4 expansion operators, requires target_host and target_port variables in path/query, supports the default MASQUE path, and expands templates into HTTP/3 scheme, authority, and path/query components. `Http3ConnectUdpTarget` validates non-empty target hosts, rejects scoped IPv6 zone identifiers, constrains ports to 1 through 65535, and percent-encodes IPv6 literal colons for template expansion.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice is pure request-contract validation. It does not open UDP sockets, perform DNS resolution, send HTTP requests, or proxy packets.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Template variables before the path/query are rejected.
Non-printable ASCII and non-ASCII characters are rejected before request creation.
IPv6 literal colons are percent-encoded in target_host expansion.
Invalid template configuration is rejected locally before sending to a UDP proxy.
risks: Actual CONNECT-UDP HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 request construction is left to a later slice.
UDP packet forwarding and datagram payload framing are left to later RFC 9298 slices.
This slice intentionally does not depend on a general URI Template library.
